subject: Cloud procurement options and marketplace path — Solaris Health post-call
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
To: Tom Liu <tom.liu@solarishealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 May 2028 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Cloud procurement options and marketplace path — Solaris Health post-call

Hi Tom — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment on procurement path (AWS Marketplace vs PO/card) and what procurement will need from us.

Call recap (30 min):
- Use case: clinical documentation assist for outpatient clinics (70% read/write).
- Priority: predictable unit economics and SOC2/DPA for PHI-adjacent logs.
- Preference signal: Infrastructure team tentative on AWS region us-west-2; finance wants a clean procurement path.

Open questions we flagged:
1) Does procurement prefer a Marketplace private offer or a direct PO? Any internal org constraints (centralized procurement card restrictions)?
2) Do you have an incumbent process for private offers / vendor onboarding in the AWS Marketplace?
3) Desired billing cadence and PO terms (Net 30 / Net 60 / prepaid)?

Suggested next steps (quick):
- Can you loop in your procurement contact (if different from this thread) and share the standard SaaS PO template?
- We’ll send a short procurement packet: SOC2 report, DPA, sample PO language, and an optional private-offer guide for Marketplace.
- Proposed timeline: provide docs by EOD Wed (5/22); procurement to confirm preferred buy path by end of next week.

Attachments: postcall-notes-solaris.pdf (post-call notes + config questions)

If helpful, Ben can map the exact Marketplace steps and provide an example private-offer contract cadence. Thanks — look forward to next steps.

—
Camila Reyes
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwood.com | +1-415-555-0192
redwood.com
From: Tom Liu <tom.liu@solarishealth.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@solarishealth.com>
Date: Tue, 21 May 2028 09:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Cloud procurement options and marketplace path — Solaris Health post-call

Thanks Camila — really helpful recap. A few quick answers and clarifications from my side.

- Procurement path: We prefer to evaluate Marketplace private offer first if it provides equivalent commercial terms — it simplifies internal approvals for our cloud spend. If Marketplace PO flow is not possible, we will route via a standard PO through our centralized purchasing system.
- Marketplace experience: we’ve used AWS Marketplace private offers before (two vendors last year). Our legal team wants to review DPA and data handling clauses early.
- Billing cadence: Preference is Net 30 but can consider Net 45 for larger annual commitments.

Looping in Procurement above to confirm who will own the PO vs Marketplace decision. Procurement, if you can confirm: what docs do you need to make the Marketplace private-offer route workable? Any specific PO language skeptically enforced?

Appreciate the pack you offered — please make sure SOC2 scope and DPA are front-and-center. Also attaching the procurement intake we usually fill: vendor-onboarding-questions.pdf (note: attached here).

Best,
Tom
Director of Infrastructure, Solaris Health
Tom.Liu@solarishealth.com | +1-510-555-2210

Subject: Re: Cloud procurement options and marketplace path — Solaris Health post-call

Tom — great context, thanks. A few practical notes on options from the Redwood side: 

1) Marketplace private offer path (preferred for Solaris if legal is comfortable):
   - We can issue a private offer in AWS Marketplace that maps to the same SKU/plan you test on. Procurement signatures are simpler because the charge shows as marketplace spend.
   - Timeline: once legal approves DPA & SOW, we can create private offer in ~3 business days.

2) Direct PO path (traditional):
   - We can accept a PO to Redwood with Net 30/45 terms. Our standard PO flow uses our SaaS PO template (attached).
   - If Solaris requires custom indemnity/data language, that will need legal involvement and may extend timeline.

Practical recommendation: run a short 1–3 month pilot on card or Marketplace test listing to validate latency/cost with a small token budget, then transition to either Marketplace private offer or PO once procurement/legal confirms terms. That approach keeps the project moving while procurement finishes approval.

Action items (who owns):
- Camila: send SOC2 + DPA + sample PO language by EOD Wed (5/22) — DONE (pack attached).
- Tom: confirm procurement owner and whether AWS Marketplace private offers are acceptable by EOW (5/26).
- Ben: will prepare a short Marketplace private-offer guide and sample order flow (link below).

Marketplace quick links: https://marketplace.aws.amazon.com/partners/marketplace?ref=redwood-inference

Attaching: marketplace-private-offer-guide.pdf, SaaS-PO-template.docx

—
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1-650-555-0177
From: Procurement <procurement@solarishealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>, Tom Liu <tom.liu@solarishealth.com>
Date: Wed, 22 May 2028 14:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Cloud procurement options and marketplace path — Solaris Health post-call

Ben/Camila — thanks for the clear options. Procurement here — a few items we need to proceed: 

1) Formal quote (line-item pricing) and confirmation of billing entity (Redwood Inc. vs Redwood Inference LLC) so we can map to our vendor master.
2) Sample PO language (attached SaaS-PO-template.docx) — please confirm if you accept our standard PO clauses or propose redlines.
3) SOC2 report and DPA — we need the most recent SOC2 Type II (preferably 2027/2028 report) and a Data Processing Addendum that covers our PHI-adjacent processing controls.

If the private-offer path is used, ensure the private offer includes equivalent legal terms or confirm that Redwood will take the Marketplace contract + our PO as supplemental terms. Either route is acceptable; Marketplace private offer is preferred for speed if we can match the above requirements.

Timeline: legal review begins 5/29; please get the quote + documents to us by COB 5/24 to be included in that packet.

Attachments: SaaS-PO-template.docx

Procurement Team
Solaris Health
